title: Light That Is Not Even: Local Thresholds and the Integral Image

questions.question: A bench lamp lights the left of a frame dimly and the right brightly. Why can no single threshold separate dark marks from the background?
options: A mark on the bright side is lighter than plain background on the dim side
questions.explanation: One threshold found 0.582 of the marks and marked 0.446 of everything else. The question per pixel is whether it is darker than its neighbours.

questions.question: What makes the sum of any rectangle cost four reads?
questions.explanation: Entry (x, y) is the sum of everything above and to the left, so a box is four entries added and subtracted. The table is built once in one pass.

questions.question: A box centred at the corner sticks out of the picture. What should its mean divide by?
options: The count of pixels actually inside the picture
questions.explanation: 81 of the 17 by 17 box, giving 90.0 on a flat picture of 90. Dividing by the whole box lowers the mean towards the border, so marks there are missed.

questions.question: What happens when the window is smaller than a mark?
options: The window averages the mark with itself and sees nothing odd
questions.explanation: A radius of 1 found only 0.317 of the marks. The window must be bigger than the mark.

questions.question: What happens when the window is as wide as the picture?
options: It is a global threshold again
questions.explanation: Radius 100 found 0.577 and marked 0.405, nearly the same as one Otsu threshold. Between the two, 8 to 16 here, it works.

questions.question: What does the offset do on a noisy picture?
options: Asks a pixel to be darker than the mean by a margin
questions.explanation: Noise is not marked: with noise of 6 levels, 0 marked 0.269 of the background and 20 marked 0.001 while finding 0.987. Choose it below the marks' contrast and above the noise.
